Rule 30: preposition plus construct noun fused into one English word before, headed on the lexeme-bearing morpheme.

The preposition is rendered *as in*, headed on *as*; taking *in* as a separate supplied word licensed by nothing is also defensible.

Head on 'near' by rule 44's subtraction: 'come' alone loses the nearness that is qrb's lexeme. Reading 'come near' as verb plus phrasal particle, which would head on 'come', remains defensible.

Anarthrous participle; the supplied 'those that' belongs to it, not to any article.

The ASV recasts 'oppressors of the hire of a hired man' so that the hireling is the object and the hire becomes 'in his wages'; the supplied 'in his' belongs to that recasting. Reading the chain with rule 19 instead is defensible.
No article morpheme in the chain, so the supplied 'the' goes with the noun (rule 29).
'turn aside' is verb plus phrasal particle and heads on the verb (rule 44); the supplied relative 'that' belongs to the participle.
The ASV supplies 'from his right' to complete the verb; no morpheme licenses it.
The ASV writes 'and ... not' separately, so no fusion to 'Nor'.

review_notes: s029/s030: the ASV's recasting of sekar sakir as 'the hireling in his wages' inverts the construct chain, so the hire takes 'in his wages' and the hired man takes the object slot.

Explicit subject pronoun, so ye is its own unit rather than the verb's (rule 17); the vocative ye of rule 36 is not in play here.

The ASV recasts 'ad bli day' as a result clause; the preposition is what the 'that' realizes. Marking it unrepresented and folding the 'that' into the day unit remains defensible.

The verbless clause's supplied copula and dummy subject join the predicate (rules 20, 34); 'room enough to receive it' is the multi-word rendering of day, headed on 'enough', which carries the lexeme (rule 31). The italicized 'to receive it' is licensed by day rather than added (rule 7), though treating it as added is defensible.
The suffix carries the pronoun; sakes is the English supplied to complete for your sakes.
The ASV writes rebuke the devourer with a bare object, leaving the b of gaar b nothing to say (rule 40).
The ASV recasts the dative of disadvantage as a possessive on ground, leaving the preposition unrendered (rule 40).

The substantival adjective is anarthrous, so the ASV's supplied 'the' belongs to the noun's own unit rather than being added.

The ASV recasts the possessive clause with the single word 'mine', which realizes the suffix; the preposition keeps no English word (rule 40).

The ASV fronts the object complement as 'even mine own possession'; the supplied 'even', 'mine' and 'own' are what the accusative licenses (rules 31, 33), and no other morpheme licenses them. Marking 'even' 'added' on the strength of the italics (rule 7) remains defensible.
